title: A Beautiful Mind — How the Film Makes Reality and Perception Compete
framing: 70% Active Cinematic Framing (1080x1344) with Ambient Blur Backdrop

beats.narration_text: A Beautiful Mind does something unusual. It makes you believe in the same reality that its main character believes in.
beats.visual_description: John Nash walking through Princeton campus, observing patterns and light refractions, establishing his brilliant, seemingly objective world.

beats.narration_text: From the moment John Nash arrives at Princeton, the camera locks onto his subjective perspective. The film doesn't use warped lenses or spooky music.
beats.visual_description: Nash scribbling equations across the dormitory window glass; camera holds a completely steady, naturalistic medium shot without horror tropes.

beats.narration_text: His roommate Charles isn't framed as a ghost—he shares drinks, gives advice, and feels completely grounded.
beats.visual_description: Charles Herman entering the room with a flask, sitting on furniture, physically interacting with the space and speaking with vibrant charm.

beats.narration_text: When a secret agent recruits Nash for Cold War codebreaking, the film frames it as a grounded espionage thriller. Because the story feels coherent, we trust it completely.
beats.visual_description: William Parcher (Ed Harris) meeting Nash in a rainy military warehouse, handing him classified orders; classic 1950s spy thriller lighting and tone.

beats.narration_text: Then comes the shock: the roommate, the agent, the conspiracy—none of them existed outside Nash's mind. It forces you to mentally rewind every earlier scene.
beats.visual_description: Dr. Rosen in the psychiatric facility and Alicia discovering the shed filled with thousands of unopened classified letters; shattering the viewer's assumed reality.

beats.narration_text: The cleverest part isn't that Nash cannot distinguish what he experiences from reality. It's that the film makes us trust his perspective before we realize we should question it.
beats.visual_description: Older John Nash walking through Princeton courtyard, seeing Charles, Marcee, and Parcher standing silent in the sun; he acknowledges them and walks into the light with Alicia.
